fatal_errors: The proposed SFE/twinning mechanism misses the target mechanisms: MSAD-controlled solid-solution strengthening, cryogenic dislocation inertia, and high-temperature dynamic solute pinning.

The investigation uses room-temperature tensile tests on thermomechanically processed polycrystalline material rather than temperature-dependent compression of oriented FCC single crystals with CRSS, strain-rate-jump, TEM, and DFT measurements.
The prediction that higher SFE intrinsically gives higher yield strength is not generally established and is supplied without evidence.
No prior supporting evidence is cited, despite the request for evidence supporting the hypothesis.
The hypothesis cannot explain the observed cryogenic CRSS dulling or the composition-dependent high-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier strengthening.
explanation: The response identifies a testable composition–structure–property idea and proposes independent SFE measurements, but it is largely orthogonal to the hidden study. The target compares slip CRSS over 9–1373 K in identically oriented single crystals and attributes composition effects primarily to lattice distortion/MSAD, phonon-drag-controlled inertia, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell pinning. Its TEM result specifically found essentially unchanged CrFeNi dissociation width/SFE after high-temperature deformation, arguing against the relevant Suzuki-segregation interpretation. The quinary baseline and FCC scope are mentioned only generically. The falsification rule is clear enough to be testable, but composition simultaneously changes many variables, so the proposed design would not isolate SFE without stronger controls.
